figure.name: Rosa Luxemburg
figure.role: Revolutionary socialist writer focused on mass action, democracy, party power, and criticism of authoritarian methods.
whyHere: Luxemburg belongs here because she shows that revolutionary socialism also contained democratic and anti-authoritarian arguments from inside the left.
She matters because the map has to separate socialism, Leninism, party-state rule, mass democracy, and anti-communist shorthand instead of flattening them together.
figure.cleanIdea: A movement for liberation has to preserve participation, dissent, and accountability while it fights for power.

hallCard.timelineMeaning: A revolutionary socialist argument insists that mass participation, dissent, and democracy cannot be treated as optional.

ideas.title: Socialist Democracy
ideas.plainDefinition: Socialist democracy means socialist politics that preserves participation, dissent, accountability, and democratic control.
ideas.context: In the Luxemburg path, democracy is not decoration. It is part of what makes socialism emancipatory rather than administrative command.
ideas.whyMatters: Socialist democracy matters because it gives the page a left-wing democratic critique of centralized party rule.

ideas.title: Mass Strike
ideas.plainDefinition: A mass strike is broad worker action that links economic pressure, political demands, organization, and public power.
ideas.context: In the Luxemburg path, mass action is how ordinary people become political actors rather than spectators.
ideas.whyMatters: Mass strike matters because it makes democracy active: people organize, stop work, assemble, and force public questions into view.

ideas.title: Democratic Dissent
ideas.plainDefinition: Democratic dissent means the protected ability to criticize leaders, parties, policies, and institutions without being treated as an enemy of society.
ideas.context: In the Luxemburg path, dissent is a test of whether a movement trusts the people it claims to represent.
ideas.whyMatters: Democratic dissent matters because truth-first politics cannot work if criticism is treated as sabotage by default.
